newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurd group slams PKK over Iraq fighting.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd group slams PKK over Iraq fighting.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish faction on Thursday slammed separatist Turkish Kurds for turning northern Iraq into a battleground, one day after Turkish troops poured into the region in pursuit of the rebels.

"We have repeatedly urged the PKK (Kurdistan Workers Party) not to establish military bases inside Iraqi Kurdistan to avoid another crisis in the area, since their domain of activity is not there," the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) said in a statement faxed to news agencies on Thursday.
"Yet the PKK did not heed our requests and consequently have turned the region once again into a battleground where the real victims would be the population of the border region."
Thousands of Turkish troops, backed by tanks, artillery and air power, moved into northern Iraq before dawn on Wednesday following a lengthy buildup.
Turkish troops often attack PKK bases in northern Iraq, but this is mostly in the form of bombing missions by jets based outside the main southeast Turkish city of Diyarbakir.
Defence Minister Turhan Tayan said the Iraq operation -- the biggest since a 35,000-man, six-week incursion in 1995 -- was a "humanitarian mission" to protect Iraqi Kurds from the PKK.
He said the assault was mounted at the invitation of KDP leader Massoud Barzani, whose peshmerga guerrillas control the Iraqi side of the border.
KDP officials would not comment on whether the Turks had come in at their behest, but demanded that the PKK leave the region.

"We in the KDP call upon the PKK once again to stop using Iraqi Kurdistan as a sanctuary for its military activity and end its presence in the border areas so the indigenous people could return to their homes and live in peace and security," said the KDP statement.
